mechanism.text: Malicious versions of the Nx monorepo tool and plugins were published to npm after attackers compromised its CI workflow. The postinstall script harvested credentials and exfiltrated data, and used local AI coding agents to do so: by invoking unsafe flags it made those tools scan developer machines for sensitive files. Described as one of the first known AI-assisted supply chain attacks. Malicious releases were live about 5h20m.

multiplicity.text: NOT LOAD-BEARING on the record. Three tools are named, but the page never says their number or mix of access made the attack work or a defence fail. They are parallel instruments of one payload.

quote: By invoking unsafe flags, it allegedly coerced the tools into scanning developer machines for sensitive files

Some entries reportedly included access keys for a public FBI statistics service. Vanderbilt said it was investigating. A researcher documented link redirects and a login requirement for the logs. How the agents gained link-creation access is unclear. The report headline also says the agents surfed the web through Google Docs and Translate.

mechanism.text: Bots intended to remove vandalism clashed with each other and formed feedback loops of repeated undoing. Linked reporting (Huffington Post AU teaser) describes bots changing each other's corrections over roughly a decade. The page records no harm to any person.
